sampling_model.design: The schedule \(g_n\), wedge \(\Omega_n\), dimensions, rank, and noise variance are fixed and known. The rate-optimal constructive theorem is restricted to the balanced rank-one one-block L-mask.
sampling_model.units: The parameter at index \(n\) is the tuple \(\vartheta_n=(L_n,D_n)\) in \(\Theta_n\), not an observational equivalence class of outcome laws.
sampling_model.treatment: The matrix \(D_n\) is supported on \(W_n\); the counterfactual target is the \(L_n\) coordinate of the same experiment index.
sampling_model.overlap: The full class imposes quantitative observed-subblock Grams. The proved rate certificate uses the single balanced chart, for which the row and column anchors are the observed half-panels and synchronization is the identity.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The total procedure randomizes the observed vector into independent Gaussian pilot and inference copies, uses total spectral and pseudoinverse conventions, applies one-step block transport, and calibrates an explicitly ordered conditional Gaussian nuclear quantile plus the homogeneous observable remainder \(\mathscr R_n^{(2)}\). The stable branch requires \(\widehat\delta_n\ge4\tau_n\); every failure triggers a deterministic covering radius. The \(\sigma\sqrt n\) expected-radius guarantee is asserted only for the balanced one-chart benchmark.
sampling_model.randomness: Under \(\mathbb P_{\vartheta,n}\), cells are independent \(\mathcal N(L_{n,it}+D_{n,it},\sigma^2)\); the main observed experiment is its \(P_{\Omega_n}Y_n\) marginal \(\mathbb Q_{\vartheta,n}\).

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorems 1--2 give entrywise Gaussian inference and a matching scalar instance-wise lower bound under staggered adoption.
Theorems 1 and 4 derive nuclear detection boundaries and nuclear-diameter rank-adaptation impossibility in Gaussian trace regression.
Theorems 3.4--3.5 characterize worst-case Frobenius residual error for nuclear-norm minimization with one missing block.
Proposition 2 derives tall-wide common-component error expansions under strong factors in the observed subblocks.
The paper constructs prescribed-coverage intervals for individual effects and bilinear functionals under staggered adoption.
The paper gives rate-optimal recovery and asymptotic normality for average treatment effects under general intervention patterns.

body.tldr: The paper indexes the Gaussian panel experiment by admissible tuples \(\vartheta_n=(L_n,D_n)\), so the latent counterfactual matrix remains part of the experiment index even when tuples induce the same observed law. Its principal interior benchmark is the balanced rank-one L-mask frontier \(\rho_{\alpha,n}^{\star}\asymp\sigma\sqrt n\) for \(\mu>1\), established by an all-procedure lower bound and a total polynomial-time one-block certificate whose conditional Gaussian, finite-simulation, homogeneous Taylor, and fallback contributions are controlled separately. Theorem \ref{thm:general-wedge-boundary-obstruction} is the indispensable boundary companion: at \(\mu=\kappa=1\), the admissible factor signs are locally discrete, an honest polynomial-time radius is \(O(\sigma)\), and the unrestricted tangent modulus remains of order \(\sigma\sqrt n\). Thus neither the interior frontier nor a tangent-modulus lower comparison extends to that boundary. Matching the tangent modulus over arbitrary admissible interior wedges remains open. The diffuse-weight ATT interval is only a coverage-valid duality corollary.

project_justification.gap: Sharp staggered-panel inference is coordinatewise or functional-specific, while global matrix confidence theory uses random or isotropic measurements. No located result gives a tuple-indexed honest nuclear ball under a deterministic adoption wedge with a computable spectral radius, an all-procedure interior benchmark, and an explicit account of the active-incoherence boundary where the usual tangent geometry ceases to describe the admissible class.
project_justification.niche: Known rank, independent Gaussian cells, strong factors, and quantitative overlap Grams isolate a deterministic-wedge confidence problem with a genuine phase split: the balanced rank-one one-block L-mask has an interior regime \(\mu>1\) and a saturated boundary \(\mu=\kappa=1\).
project_justification.fill: For the balanced rank-one L-mask, Theorem \ref{thm:balanced-frontier} proves the \(\sigma\sqrt n\) two-sided frontier only in the interior regime \(\mu>1\). Its total spectral certificate is audited term by term, including the homogeneous Taylor remainder and the large-gap fallback tail. Theorem \ref{thm:general-wedge-boundary-obstruction} proves the boundary phase change: when \(\mu=\kappa=1\), a polynomial-time uniformly honest procedure has radius \(O(\sigma)\), while the unrestricted tangent modulus is at least \(\sigma\sqrt{2n}\), so that modulus cannot furnish a uniform minimax lower comparison. The overlap-aligned tangent-packing question remains open only for arbitrary admissible interior wedges.

body.related_work: Yan and Wainwright provide the closest computational and inferential construction: their four-block SVD estimator has non-asymptotic entrywise Gaussian approximations and matching scalar lower bounds. Bai and Ng supply the tall-wide factor-rotation architecture and asymptotic counterfactual expansions under strong observed subblocks; block transport is used here as a supporting identification lemma. Carpentier and Nickl supply a testing reduction for honest nuclear confidence diameter, but their experiment is isotropic Gaussian trace regression and their central obstruction is rank adaptation. Capponi and Stojnic analyze worst-case Frobenius residuals and phase transitions for nuclear-norm minimization with one missing block; their loss and procedure-specific target differ from the uniformly honest radius. Chen, Fan, Ma, and Yan provide debiased uncertainty quantification under random sampling, where sampling isometry replaces deterministic block geometry. Chatterjee characterizes qualitative recoverability under arbitrary deterministic masks. Arkhangelsky and Imbens organize factor and assignment-pattern distinctions but report no global honest matrix radius. Against these comparators, Theorem \ref{thm:balanced-frontier} supplies the \(\mu>1\) interior \(\sigma\sqrt n\) frontier, whereas Theorem \ref{thm:general-wedge-boundary-obstruction} shows that at \(\mu=\kappa=1\) the honest radius can be \(O(\sigma)\) even though the unrestricted tangent modulus is order \(\sigma\sqrt n\); neither comparison should be read across that boundary. Xia, Yan, and Wainwright and Farias, Li, and Peng are functional-specific benchmarks for weighted effects; the ATT proposition claims coverage transfer and no optimal-length comparison.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The \(\sigma\sqrt n\) certificate and minimax frontier are confined to the balanced rank-one one-block L-mask. The displayed multi-chart synchronization remains a total computational construction, but no rate or honesty theorem is asserted for a general connected wedge. A broader theorem would need a uniform post-synchronization envelope and nuclear-mask amplification bound, together with a same-class tangent packing that preserves exact rank, strong factors, incoherence, and controlled observed-law divergence.
body.honest_scope: The balanced rank-one two-sided frontier, its total one-block spectral certificate, and the diffuse-weight ATT coverage corollary are theorem targets. The exact conditional Gaussian term, Monte Carlo inflation, homogeneous Taylor remainder, and fallback contribution are each bounded at the \(\sigma\sqrt n\) benchmark scale. Both a polynomial-time rate-optimal certificate and a matching all-procedure lower bound for arbitrary quantitatively admissible wedges remain open in Open-ended Question 1. No theorem is asserted for a multi-chart connected wedge, unknown rank, approximate low rank, dependent or heteroskedastic errors, adaptive adoption, or optimal ATT length. In the noiseless one-chart case, the supporting block-transport lemma reduces to exact tall-wide transport.
